findings.evidence: Structured output adds another gate: an API that documents JSON-schema generation and a self-hosted backend that rejects grammar constraints are not interchangeable candidates.3
findings.issue: The footnote marker 3 attaches a claim about structured-output/grammar-constraint behavior to sources that are dated 2026-10-28, outside the stated 2026-08-30 evidence cutoff. The text does not flag the claim as a post-cutoff addendum at the point of use, even though the footnote itself admits the sources are post-cutoff.
findings.fix_instruction: Add an inline post-cutoff/addendum note where the structured-output claim is made, or move the claim to the addendum section so it is not presented as part of the August 2026 evidence snapshot.

findings.evidence: Page 100, §5.3(b): "prefill dominates the linear FLOP budget (~97% of tokens and linear FLOPs) while decode dominates single-stream wall-clock (~85% of 7.08 s on the illustrative 20 ms/token basis… ~87% of 8.58 s on the canonical 25 ms/token basis…) — the two percentages are the same quantity at two different operating points, not one series".
findings.issue: The text says 'the two percentages are the same quantity at two different operating points' — but 85% and 87% are wall-clock shares of decode under two different TPOT budgets (20 ms/token vs 25 ms/token). They are the same *metric* (decode share of total request time) at two *operating points*, which the text correctly states. However, the parenthetical already says 'not one series' — and then the main sentence says 'the same quantity' — these two clauses say slightly different things ('not one series' implies they shouldn't be trended together; 'same quantity' implies they are directly comparable). The double qualification ('same quantity… not one series') is redundant and slightly confusing in sequence.
findings.fix_instruction: Simplify to one qualifier: 'the two percentages are decode shares at two different operating points and should not be compared as if they were one series' — or delete the redundant second qualifier.

findings.evidence: Page 98, §5.3(a): "~186–371 ms if encoded on a single CPU core at ~30–60 GFLOP/s sustained… but only ~1.1 ms on a ~10 TFLOP/s GPU". Deltas: 14.08 − 2.94 = 11.14 GFLOP. Check: 11.14 ÷ 30 = 0.3713 s = 371 ms ✓; 11.14 ÷ 60 = 0.1857 s = 186 ms ✓; 11.14 ÷ 10,000,000 = 0.001114 s = 1.11 ms ✓.
findings.issue: The arithmetic checks out for all three values (371 ms, 186 ms, 1.1 ms). No arithmetic defect. However, the text states 'single-core encoding fits only above ≈92.8 GFLOP/s sustained per core (11.14 GFLOP ÷ 0.12 s)' — check: 11.14 ÷ 0.12 = 92.83 GFLOP/s ✓. The threshold is correctly derived. The [HYPOTHESIS] label on the original latency claim is appropriate since no measurement is cited. No defect in this passage — arithmetic verified and label appropriate.
findings.fix_instruction: No fix needed; arithmetic and labels verified correct.

findings.evidence: "[1P][HYPOTHESIS]: for the canonical 2,000-user workload with ~10 rps average, the incremental per-request compute cost of the 768-dim (all-mpnet) vs 384-dim (MiniLM) embedding models — a cross-model difference, not a dim-only sweep — is ~11.1 GFLOP per 64-token query (2 × params × L: 14.08 − 2.94 GFLOP, the Table 5-1 embedding table's own rows)." Preface, PDF p. 21 (printed p. xvii): "Arithmetic belongs on the epistemic-status axis, not the provenance axis: a worked example computed from a model card is [1P][DERIVED], never [2°]."
findings.issue: The 11.1 GFLOP figure is pure arithmetic on two model-card parameter counts (Table 5-1's own [1P][FACT] rows), so its epistemic status is DERIVED, not HYPOTHESIS ("reasoned but not yet validated"). The sentence also mixes canonical-scenario inputs (2,000 users, 10 rps) into a row whose Axis-1 provenance is declared as first-party.
findings.fix_instruction: Relabel the GFLOP delta as [1P][DERIVED] (and move the canonical-workload framing into a separate [canonical scenario] clause); keep [1P][HYPOTHESIS] only for the genuinely open claim that the ~15% MAP uplift transfers to the target corpus.

findings.page: PDF p. 125 (printed p. 101); PDF p. 133 (printed p. 109)
findings.evidence: Ch. 5 §5.3(b): "Within the 1.2 s TTFT budget, prefill (9.2K tokens) takes ~1.08 s and the retrieval allocation is ~120 ms, leaving zero true headroom on that two-term model". Ch. 5 §5.8: "The prefill TTFT of ~1.08 s plus retrieval (~120 ms) sits at the 1.2 s TTFT budget". Table 4-2 (PDF p. 98, printed p. 74): "Prefill compute budget — two-term-only upper cap, NOT a feasible deployed prefill target ... Treat 1.08 s as an upper reach (a real deployed prefill budget is smaller), not an achievable allocation". Ch. 4 (PDF p. 80, printed p. 80): "budget cap 1.08 s ... — a budget, not a modeled runtime ... The modeled host prefill is ~0.16 s at peak and ~0.47 s at 35% MFU".
findings.issue: Cross-chapter status conflict for a load-bearing number: 1.08 s is a budget cap in Ch. 4/Table 4-2 and is described as a measured/assumed prefill runtime ("takes ~1.08 s") in Ch. 5, which also omits the book-wide caveat that the cap must be written as "budget_prefill ≤ 1.08 s − B_other". The two statements are ~2.3× apart in what they imply about the modelled host prefill (0.47 s vs 1.08 s).
findings.fix_instruction: Reword both Ch. 5 passages to keep the budget/measurement distinction, e.g. "the prefill budget cap is 1.08 s (modelled host prefill ≈0.47 s at 35% MFU; the cap leaves no allowance for admission/queue or tokenization/transfer)".

findings.evidence: "leaving zero true headroom on that two-term model (admission/queueing, tokenization/transfer, network transit, scheduling and first-token sampling sit outside it)" vs the defining convention (p. 40): "It carries no separate 'first decode step' term: under the convention above, the first token's forward pass is sampled inside prefill, so a term for it would count that work twice."
findings.issue: The sentence lists 'first-token sampling' as a term outside the retrieval+prefill budget, directly contradicting the book's defining TTFT convention (stated in the Preface p. 22 and Ch 2 p. 40) under which first-token sampling is inside prefill. It also invents 'network transit' and 'scheduling' as decomposition terms that do not exist in the canonical four-term formula (retrieval + admission/queue + tokenization/transfer + prefill).
findings.fix_instruction: Delete 'first-token sampling' from the outside-terms list and restrict the enumeration to the canonical remaining terms (admission/queue and tokenization/transfer), or explicitly note any additional unmodeled terms as extensions beyond the defined formula.

findings.evidence: "[ILLUSTRATIVE][HYPOTHESIS]: guardrail latency (PII redaction, refusal checking) on generated 300-token outputs, ~2–8 ms/request on CPU at this chapter's scenario inputs; measure on the target stack (the figure depends on the guardrail implementation and hardware)." vs Note 1 (p. 100): "a hypothesis is tagged [HYPOTHESIS] (Axis 2), never [ILLUSTRATIVE] (Axis 1)" and the Axis-2 definition (p. 20): "ASSUMPTION — a deliberately chosen scenario input".
findings.issue: The ~2–8 ms range is a chosen scenario input (the sentence itself says 'at this chapter's scenario inputs'), which the taxonomy assigns to ASSUMPTION, not HYPOTHESIS ('reasoned but not yet validated'); the [ILLUSTRATIVE][HYPOTHESIS] pairing is additionally banned verbatim by Note 1 of Table 4-2. (Related hygiene: the same section tags a negative-existence claim '[1P][HYPOTHESIS]', a provenance no source can supply.)
findings.fix_instruction: Retag the guardrail-latency item as [ILLUSTRATIVE][ASSUMPTION] (it becomes HYPOTHESIS only if a mechanism argument, rather than a chosen range, is offered), and drop the [1P] partner from hypothesis-only claims or name the first-party source that motivates them.

findings.evidence: "(Mixed-input convention: when a derivation mixes a canonical price with an illustrative rate, the result carries the non-canonical provenance — here the 50 tok/s rate input is [ILLUSTRATIVE][ASSUMPTION] while the $20/hr price is canonical (Table 4‑2, a dated price snapshot, [canonical scenario][ASSUMPTION]).)" vs the front matter's claim (p. 5): "The axes and the full label set are defined in the Preface".
findings.issue: The mixed-input dominance rule — which governs every per-dollar result in Table 5-2 and the §5.3.2 economics — is introduced only as a mid-book parenthetical and appears nowhere in the Preface's evidence-discipline panel that the front matter designates as the definition layer for the label system. A reader applying the Preface alone would not know mixed derivations inherit the non-canonical tag.
findings.fix_instruction: Add the mixed-input dominance rule to the Preface's Evidence boundary panel (one sentence next to the ASSUMPTION/DERIVED mapping), with a pointer to the Ch 5 worked instance.

findings.evidence: "~85% of 7.08 s on the illustrative 20 ms/token basis — 6.0 s decode of 1.08 s prefill + 6.0 s decode" and, parallel, "~87% of 8.58 s on the canonical 25 ms/token basis — 7.5 s decode of 1.08 s prefill + 7.5 s decode, Ch 4".
findings.issue: Both parentheticals are malformed: '6.0 s decode of 1.08 s prefill + 6.0 s decode' states decode twice and reads as a garbled sum; the intended content is '7.08 s = 1.08 s prefill + 6.0 s decode'. As printed, the sentence asserting the wall-clock split is itself hard to parse, in the chapter's key prefill-vs-decode framing passage.
findings.fix_instruction: Rewrite both parentheticals as 'N% of the T s single-stream window (1.08 s prefill + D s decode)', e.g., '7.08 s = 1.08 s prefill + 6.0 s decode' and '8.58 s = 1.08 s prefill + 7.5 s decode'.
